parts.note: Hobnobs are a British brand of oat biscuit
what you lie and rest on is a bed

explanation.surface: Someone eats a jumble of biscuits in bed, crumbs and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like it describes the biscuits, but it is the definition, in the sense of mingling socially.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to socialise or mingle with people, so having mixed at a party is having hobnobbed.

clue.text: Upstanding monarch having welcomed posh royal couple, cheers

indicators.note: taking in guests means the other letters are put inside
in a down clue, standing up means the word for the monarch is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a shah was the monarch of Iran
U is the old label for upper-class usage
R is an abbreviation for royal, and a couple of them gives two

explanation.surface: A ruler on his feet welcomes a smart royal pair, and the crowd cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' turns SHAH into HAHS, and 'having welcomed' puts U and RR inside it after the first H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurrahs are shouts of joy or approval, the same as cheers from a crowd.

parts.note: brio is vigour or zest
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, is a stock crossword red

explanation.surface: Zest mixed with red pepper, perhaps, in a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across is BREAD, so the definition asks for a kind of bread. 'red' is a communist, here Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: Brioche is a soft enriched French loaf, a type of bread.

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: shifts means the letters of the word dangerous are moved about

explanation.surface: A watchful worker on dangerous shift patterns must stay alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like the noun for work periods but is the anagram signal: DANGEROUS rearranged gives ONESGUARD after ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's guard means staying watchful for danger, which is being alert.

parts.note: read playfully, a churchgoer of this Protestant denomination sounds like one who worships a bread roll, as a bap is a soft roll

explanation.walkthrough: 6 across is BREAD; a BAP is a British soft bread roll, so the denomination's name looks like 'bap' plus the ending of a devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Baptist church is a Christian worshipper, and the name jokily starts with a bread roll.

clue.text: A cast from woeful musical shows

parts.note: dire means dreadful or woeful

indicators.note: to cast something from a place is to throw it out, so this letter is removed

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe tours a dreadful musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests theatre performers, but 'cast from' throws the A out of DIRE CATS, leaving DIRECTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to show them the way, so shows can mean directs.

clue.text: That which has risen, raised reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for raised is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a child that is raised is bred

explanation.surface: Something gone up, or brought up, as someone has heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on dough rising as it proves.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaf is made from dough that has risen with yeast before baking.

clue.text: Opening for Bangladesh, you have a good day

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of Bangladesh

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A Bangladesh opening batsman has a good day at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture is a decoy: a bye in cricket is an extra run, but here the word is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye is a farewell, said as people part, just as 'have a good day' is.

parts.note: voters elect a candidate to bring them into office
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist is brought in to paint a soul bent on revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth she urged her brother to avenge their father's murder by killing their mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the mythical Greek princess driven to revenge for Agamemnon's death.

clue.text: China, where medic needs to undergo surgery

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: an operation on the word needs rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: In China, a doctor needs an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain: the German city gives its name to a fine porcelain. 'to undergo surgery' rearranges NEEDS into ESDEN after DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a fine porcelain made near that German city, a famous type of china.

indicators.note: mentioning means the words are spoken and heard rather than read

parts.note: rye flour is an ingredient of some bread; no is a flat refusal, never

explanation.surface: A loaf's recipe is mentioned, and someone says never!
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across is BREAD, here in its slang sense of money; RHINO is old British slang for cash too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for money, and bread is also slang for cash.

parts.note: per means for, as in price per item
severe can mean harsh or cruel

explanation.surface: A harsh boss means business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective near 'cruel', but 'Mean business' is one phrase, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going with determination, as someone who means business does.

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words, so the word is spoken the Cockney way

parts.note: hark means listen

explanation.surface: Pay attention to a Londoner's chat-up line.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, from East London, drops initial H, so HARK said that way sounds like ARC.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curved line, part of a circle's circumference.

indicators.note: counterfeit means faked, so the letters of the following words are made up into a new shape

explanation.surface: Forged artwork fools people, and so it was sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests sketching, but here it means disembowelled, as in hanged, drawn and quartered.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a bird is to remove its guts, so drawn means disembowelled.

clue.text: Honest reply having received bill after cut off

annotationWithheld.why: Honest reply having received bill after cut off: RESPONSE takes in IBL, and no reading of 'bill after cut off' gives IBL in that order
annotationWithheld.clue: Honest reply having received bill after cut off

indicators.note: a recital is something spoken aloud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: slight means small or negligible

explanation.surface: A performer's skill barely shows in a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recital' looks like a musical performance; here it means saying aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity or cunning skill, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: One trapped by Texan brown bear?

parts.note: a Texan is from the southern US, S and US

indicators.note: something trapped by other letters is shut inside them

parts.note: tan is a light brown
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One person is caught by a Texan brown bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb, to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a weight or hardship is to sustain or support it.

clue.text: Keen to eat turkey, give Christmas performance?

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief
a turkey is slang for a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Someone eager to eat the turkey puts on a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager but is the verb, to lament loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To wassail is to go from house to house carol singing at Christmas.

indicators.note: to make a balls of something is to mess it up, so these letters are jumbled
emptying the word with leaves just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fellow players with deflated footballs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teammates' must be split: TEAM is the definition and MATES joins the first and last letters of 'with' as fodder. WEST HAM is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: West Ham United is a London football club, a team.

clue.text: Slave elected to consume energy drink

indicators.note: to consume something is to take it inside

parts.note: to slave is to toil or slog
E is the symbol for energy in physics
a winning candidate is voted in

explanation.surface: An elected drudge downs an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slave' is the verb, to work hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloe gin is a liqueur made by steeping sloes in gin, a drink.

parts.note: lil is a casual form of little
in Jamaican speech, thing is said as ting

explanation.surface: A small musical item from Jamaica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item from Jamaica' sounds like a reggae track, but means THING as spoken in Jamaican English.
explanation.definitionFit: A lilting tune has a pleasant swinging rhythm, so it is melodious.

definitions.meaning: 6 across is bread: a large crusty white loaf
a blunder or mistake, a lapse

explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is both a long crusty loaf of bread and a silly mistake.

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a run is a race

explanation.surface: A process undone in the second heat of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like a position or time but is the verb, to support.
explanation.definitionFit: A backrun is a process run in reverse, going back over the steps.

clue.text: Dangerous chemical a corporation dug up, all one needs to know

indicators.note: in a down clue, dug up means these letters rise, read from bottom to top

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A firm unearthed a toxic substance, and that is all you need to know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug up' turns A TUM into MUTA; 'corporation' is a jokey old word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutagen is an agent that causes genetic mutation, a harmful substance.

parts.note: to phone is to ring

indicators.note: two ways of taking one word, the second read backwards

parts.note: tel is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: A security lock on a phone that works both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-way' asks for 'phone' twice: once as RING, once as TEL read backwards, LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.

clue.text: 6 across, pound wasted pumping up tyres

indicators.note: pumping air into tyres puts something inside them

parts.note: slicks are smooth racing tyres

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters of pound are reshaped

explanation.surface: A pound is squandered on inflating tyres.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across BREAD means money here; 'wasted' rearranges POUND into PONDU inside SLICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spondulicks is British slang for money, as bread is.

definitions.meaning: bread in its slang sense of money
a loaf is baked in a metal mould

explanation.definitionFit: Tin is old slang for money and also a baking tin holds a loaf.

parts.note: someone drugged is high

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, so the letters of rifle are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gun fired by a stoned live wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dynamo' is an energetic, successful person, not a generator.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-flier is an ambitious achiever, a dynamo.

indicators.note: oddly keeps only the odd-placed letters, so the second and fourth go

parts.note: Ali Baba faced forty thieves

explanation.surface: A gang of robbers cooks strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: The number comes from the tale of Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: To fry is to cook in hot fat.

indicators.note: returned means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: LE, French for the, plus GAB, the Irish gift of the gab

explanation.surface: A present from France and Ireland is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: The gift of the gab, fluent talk, is a stereotype of the Irish; Le is French for the.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll.

clue.text: 6 across I fed to holy Moses

indicators.note: something fed to another goes inside it

parts.note: an exclamation of surprise, like my!
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims holy Moses after being fed bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across BREAD means money here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money.

clue.text: Whisk egg in and turn liquid for biscuit

indicators.note: whisking stirs up, so the letters of egg in are mixed
liquid means fluid, so the letters of turn flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe step: beat an egg in and make it runny for the biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: EGG IN rearranges to GINGE and TURN to RNUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingernut is a hard ginger-flavoured British biscuit.
